features.limits: The condition must be compile-time constant and effect-free.
features.accepted_example:
VALUE :: #run 41 + 1
#assert VALUE == 42
#program_export
Answer :: () -> s32 { return VALUE }
features.rejection: A false compile-time assertion fails checking.

features.syntax: #law NAME theorem bindings => condition; #proof NAME { steps; }
features.limits: The kernel checks booleans, fixed-width modular integers, enum equality, and acyclic pure scalar procedures. Unsupported code and exhausted budgets are unknown. custom checks one example; forall checks a finite domain.
features.rejection: An invalid certificate fails checking and cannot be waived.

features.limits: Compile-time execution is bounded and effect-free. Supported scalars, strings, records, and arrays can be evaluated; general metaprogramming and runtime effects remain unsupported.
features.rejection: Compile-time calls cannot mutate runtime storage.

target_support.limit: Forward CPU regions execute on threads.
CPU regions execute serially with a downgrade marker.
CPU regions execute serially with a downgrade marker.
CPU regions execute serially with a downgrade marker.

features.limits: Forward regions use CPU threads on C. Other targets and reverse regions run serially with a downgrade marker. Iterations may write only iteration-local storage; reductions and nested regions are unsupported.
features.rejection: Parallel iterations cannot mutate shared storage.

target_support.limit: CPU fallback only; no GPU device backend.
CPU fallback only; no GPU device backend.
CPU fallback only; no GPU device backend.
CPU fallback only; no GPU device backend.

features.limits: GPU-safe regions are checked, but execute on the CPU with an explicit downgrade marker. No GPU device backend exists. Pointer storage, pointer-bearing calls, and allocator-backed Vec mutation are rejected.
features.rejection: GPU fallback retains the checked parallel-region effect rules.

features.limits: The format must be a string literal. Each % consumes one integer, float, bool, string, enum, record, or fixed-array argument; an enum prints as its member name and a record as {x = 1, y = 2}, with strings quoted, fixed arrays up to 16 elements, and Vecs and slices by count; %% prints one percent. Arguments are evaluated left to right before output, and floats use the shortest decimal that round-trips to the same value.
features.rejection: print requires a string literal format.

features.limits: New allocates a zeroed value and free ignores null. Types holding owned Vec storage are rejected. Native callers must release allocations once and preserve pointer lifetimes; Python and the portable VM reject direct reads after free and double frees.
features.rejection: Heap allocation cannot bypass owned Vec cleanup.

features.limits: The alias exposes public declarations; it does not re-export a dependency's private names or make every transitive import visible.
features.rejection: Jai imports require a quoted module or file name.

features.syntax: Function :: (parameters) -> Result #asm("architecture[+feature...]", "template", "outputs", "inputs", "clobbers", "options") { portable body }; local #asm blocks use constraint:alias=binding operands

target_support.limit: GNU extended assembly in functions and local blocks, with isolated CPU-feature variants on x86 and Linux/Android AArch64; unsupported platforms use the portable body.

Checked Go body by default. -tags=ziran_asm enables the GNU cgo bridge with CGO_ENABLED=1, or direct AMD64 Go ABI0 for represented numeric/register-result forms with CGO_ENABLED=0. The direct path retains the checked body for pointer operands/results, stack changes, external calls/data and other unrepresented forms. Package builds include generated assembly companions; small native calls still have ABI overhead.
Executes the checked portable body; no native assembly emission.
Executes the checked portable body; no native assembly emission.

features.limits: Function variants require named scalar/pointer parameters and scalar/pointer or flat record results. Local blocks bind scalar/pointer locals or parameters; variants must bind the same names in the same order and their checked body must fall through. At most 30 input/output operands; outputs use = constraints and read/write values use tied inputs. CPU feature selection uses x86 GCC/Clang GNU-ABI drivers, Linux/Android AArch64 hardware capabilities, or direct Go ABI0 CPUID and OS register-state checks; unavailable variants use the checked body. Required features are combined with + and variants are tried in source order; duplicate/shadowed variants are rejected. Generic procedures retain assembly through specialization; operand shapes, types and portable bodies are checked for each concrete instance. asm goto, naked functions and standalone assembler files are not yet supported. Native assembly/fallback equivalence remains the author's obligation.
features.rejection: Input and output constraint counts must match parameters and results.

features.syntax: a narrower value where a wider type is expected, or mixed in a binary operator
features.limits: Only lossless conversions are implicit: a wider integer of the same signedness, an unsigned integer in a wider signed type, and float32 in float64. The checker inserts an explicit cast, so every target sees the same conversion.
features.rejection: Narrowing, sign changes, and integer-to-float conversions need an explicit cast.

features.syntax: s8, u8, s16, u16, s32, u32, s64, u64, float32, float64, and cast(T) expressions
features.limits: The stable differential matrix covers the published IDs below; broader operator and mixed-width combinations remain to be added.
features.rejection: Legacy f64 spelling is rejected; write float64.

features.limits: Locals, parameters, and Vec fields in records/fixed arrays are dropped on scope exit. Moves invalidate their source. Globals are shared storage; indexed and pointer-backed field moves still have restrictions.
features.accepted_example:
#import "vec"
#program_export
Answer :: () -> s32 {
    values: Vec(s32)
    VecPush(values, 42)
    return values[0]
}
features.rejected_example:
#import "vec"
Answer :: () -> s32 {
    values: Vec(s32)
    VecPush(values, 42)
    moved := values
    return values[0]
}
features.rejection: Owned values cannot be read after moving.

features.syntax: TextView(bytes[:]) and lexical release at view scope close

target_support.limit: Mutable backing bytes are observed as a borrow.

features.limits: Unknown heap aliases and host-backed views still need a complete lifetime model. Native and portable targets disagree when checked mutation restrictions are bypassed.
features.rejection: Mutable backing storage cannot be changed while a view of it is live.

features.syntax: record.field Vec moves from local aggregate paths
features.limits: Indexed fields, pointer-backed fields, global storage, and repeated moves in one expression remain rejected.
features.rejection: Indexed aggregate fields do not yet have a precise per-element ownership transfer.

features.syntax: Procedure :: (value: Type = expression, inferred := expression) -> Result
features.limits: Named procedures expand omitted defaults in declaration scope. Explicit arguments run before omitted defaults. Defaults on procedure-type parameters remain unsupported; generic defaults retain documented specialization limits.
features.rejected_example:
Required :: (value: s32) -> s32 { return value }
Answer :: () -> s32 { return Required() }
features.rejection: Required parameters without defaults cannot be omitted.

features.syntax: Callback :: #type (value: Type) -> Result; named capture-free procedure values
features.limits: Named procedures can be passed, stored, returned, and called through checked procedure types. Local procedures cannot capture enclosing locals. Polymorphic procedures as values and defaults on procedure-type parameters remain unsupported; native callback ABI support depends on the target.
features.rejection: Procedure values must match their checked parameter and result signature.
